Preferred regimen (3): Artesunate at a dose of 2–10 mg/kg/day orally once daily, combined with Mefloquine at a dose of 2–10 mg/kg/day orally once daily, for a duration of 3 days. 3. Dosage regimen based on body weight: For body weight 5 to <9 kg: Artesunate 25 mg orally once daily and Mefloquine 55 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 9 to <18 kg: Artesunate 50 mg orally once daily and Mefloquine 110 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 18 to <36 kg: Artesunate 100 mg orally once daily and Mefloquine 220 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight ≥36 kg: Artesunate 200 mg orally once daily and Mefloquine 440 mg orally once daily for 3 days. 4. Preferred regimen (4): Artesunate at 2–10 mg/kg/day orally once daily for 3 days, combined with Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (25–70 mg/kg/day of Sulfadoxine and 1.25–3.5 mg/kg/day of Pyrimethamine) as a single dose on day 1. 5. Dosage regimen based on body weight: For body weight 5 to <10 kg: Artesunate 25 mg orally once daily for 3 days and Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine 250/12 mg as a single dose on day 1. For body weight 10 to <25 kg: Artesunate 50 mg orally once daily for 3 days and Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine 500/25 mg as a single dose on day 1. For body weight 25 to <50 kg: Artesunate 100 mg orally once daily for 3 days and Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine 1000/50 mg as a single dose on day 1. For body weight ≥50 kg: Artesunate 200 mg orally once daily for 3 days and Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine 1500/75 mg as a single dose on day 1. 6. Preferred regimen (5): Dihydroartemisinin at 2–10 mg/kg/day orally once daily, combined with Piperaquine at 16–27 mg/kg/day orally once daily, for 3 days. 7. Dosage regimen based on body weight: For body weight 5 to <8 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 20 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 160 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 8 to <11 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 30 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 240 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 11 to <17 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 40 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 320 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 17 to <25 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 60 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 480 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 25 to <36 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 80 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 640 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 36 to <60 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 120 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 960 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight 60 to <80 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 160 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 1280 mg orally once daily for 3 days. For body weight >80 kg: Dihydroartemisinin 200 mg orally once daily and Piperaquine 1600 mg orally once daily for 3 days. 8. To reduce the transmissibility of treated Plasmodium falciparum infections in low-transmission areas (excluding pregnant women, infants <6 months, and breastfeeding women of infants <6 months), administer a single dose of 0.25 mg/kg of Primaquine in combination with ACT. 9. For recurrent Plasmodium falciparum malaria: If treatment failure occurs within 28 days, use an alternative ACT known to be effective in the region. Adherence to 7-day regimens (e.g., Artesunate or Quinine with Tetracycline, Doxycycline, or Clindamycin) is often poor without direct observation and is no longer generally recommended. If treatment failure occurs after 28 days, consider the case as a new infection and treat with the first-line ACT. Avoid reusing Mefloquine within 60 days due to increased risk of neuropsychiatric reactions; use an alternative ACT instead. 10. For uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in special risk groups: Pregnancy: First trimester: Quinine and Clindamycin at 10 mg/kg/day orally twice daily for 7 days. Second and third trimesters: Mefloquine is considered safe but should only be used in combination with an artemisinin derivative. Note: Quinine is associated with an increased risk of hypoglycemia in late pregnancy and should only be used if no effective alternatives are available. Primaquine and tetracyclines are contraindicated in pregnancy. Infants <5 kg body weight: Treat with ACT at the same mg/kg target dose as for children weighing 5 kg. HIV co-infection: Avoid Artesunate + Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine if the patient is receiving Co-trimoxazole. Avoid Artesunate + Amodiaquine if the patient is receiving Efavirenz or Zidovudine. Obese patients: Dose based on lean or ideal body weight, as less drug is distributed to fat tissue. Non-obese but heavy patients require the same mg/kg doses as lighter patients. TB co-infection: Rifamycins, particularly Rifampicin, are potent CYP3A4 inducers with weak antimalarial activity. Non-immune travelers: Treat travelers returning to non-endemic settings with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria using ACT. Uncomplicated hyperparasitemia: Patients with Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitemia are at increased risk of treatment failure, severe malaria, and death. They should be closely monitored and treated with ACT. 11. For uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax, P. ovale, P. malariae, or P. knowlesi: Blood stage infection: In areas with chloroquine-sensitive P. vivax, administer a total dose of 25 mg/kg of Chloroquine orally (10 mg/kg on day 1, 10 mg/kg on day 2, and 5 mg/kg on day 3). In areas with chloroquine-resistant P. vivax, use ACTs containing Piperaquine, Mefloquine, or Lumefantrine. Artesunate + Amodiaquine may also be effective in some areas. Dihydroartemisinin + Piperaquine provides a longer prophylactic effect compared to ACTs with shorter half-lives. Mixed malaria infections: ACTs are effective against all malaria species and are the treatment of choice for mixed infections. 12. For liver stages (hypnozoites) of P. vivax and P. ovale, additional treatment is required to prevent relapse.
